To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated that DTI analysis is sensitive to detect both focal and global abnormalities in a model of mTBI in ferret and that the combination of D-TBM and DTI ROI analysis can detect and quantify these changes.
we have developed a novel and robust model of mild TBL in the ferret that can be used for the study of mTBI.
we used diffusion tensor MRI (MRI) to study mild brain injury (mild traumatic brain injury) in a ferret model of mild brain injury (controlled cortical impact).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of novel DTI analysis tools for the detection of mTBI effects in a ferret model.
developing and validating novel MRI methods for detecting and characterizing mTBI in a gyrencephallic species that shares many features of human brain structure and function.
the development and application of DTI and DTI-driven TBM to a ferret model of mild TCI and the comparison of these findings with human mTBI data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of high resolution DTI and D-TBM analysis of the ferret CCI model is an effective tool for detecting mTBI-induced alterations in brain tissue microstructure, and that these findings can inform and support the design of human studies.
the ferret model of mTBI provides a robust, sensitive, and informative approach to the study of mild brain injury.
the combination of a ferret model of mTBI with DTI and D-TBM analysis provides a powerful and sensitive approach to investigate mTBI pathophysiology and the potential for recovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DTI is a useful and sensitive approach for detecting cellular alterations in the ferret model of mTBI.
the DTI and D-TBM tools are able to detect and distinguish mTBI effects in this model system, and the ferret model system is able to robustly recapitulate key features of human TBM.

the combination of a ferret model and DTI analysis provides a promising approach to study the cellular and structural changes that occur after mTBI and that these changes can be detected and quantified using the DTI and DTI-driven TBM analysis methods described here.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ferret is a highly suitable species for mTBI studies, especially in the context of DTI and D-TBM analysis, and the ferret model is likely to be an important tool for future research into the cellular and molecular mechanisms that underlie mTBI and the long term effects of mTBI.
DTI and D-TBM can be used to detect and quantify subtle changes in brain tissue after mild TBI in a gyrencephaly model.
DTI can be used to evaluate focal and global changes in the ferret brain after mTBI.
